name: Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs)
definition: Equations involving derivatives of a function with respect to one independent variable.
formula: dy/dx = f(x,y); General form: F(x, y, y', y'', ..., y^(n)) = 0
examples: dy/dx = ky has solution y = Ce^(kx)
y'' + 4y = 0 has solution y = C1*cos(2x) + C2*sin(2x)

name: Partial Differential Equations (PDEs)
definition: Equations involving partial derivatives of a function with respect to multiple independent variables.
formula: ∂u/∂t = k(∂²u/∂x²) (heat equation); ∂²u/∂x² + ∂²u/∂y² = 0 (Laplace equation)

name: Laplace Transform
definition: An integral transform that converts a function of time into a function of complex frequency.
examples: Solving ODEs: L{y''} = s²Y(s) - sy(0) - y'(0)

name: Fourier Series
definition: Representation of a periodic function as a sum of sine and cosine functions.
formula: f(x) = a₀/2 + Σ[aₙcos(nπx/L) + bₙsin(nπx/L)]
examples: Heat conduction with periodic boundary conditions

name: Linear System of ODEs
definition: System of differential equations that can be written in matrix form dX/dt = AX.
formula: dX/dt = AX, where X is vector, A is coefficient matrix
examples: Predator-prey models: dx/dt = ax - bxy, dy/dt = -cy + dxy
Solution involves eigenvalues λ and eigenvectors v of A

name: Vector Spaces
definition: A set of vectors with defined addition and scalar multiplication satisfying specific axioms.
formula: Axioms: closure, associativity, commutativity, identity, inverse, scalar distribution
examples: Set of all polynomials of degree ≤n

name: Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors
definition: For matrix A, eigenvector v satisfies Av = λv where λ is the eigenvalue.
formula: Av = λv; Characteristic equation: det(A - λI) = 0

name: Matrix Decompositions
definition: Factorization of a matrix into simpler matrices with special properties.
formula: LU: A = LU; QR: A = QR; SVD: A = UΣV^T; Eigendecomposition: A = PDP^(-1)
examples: LU decomposition for solving Ax = b efficiently
QR for orthogonalization and least squares
SVD for data compression and dimensionality reduction

name: Linear Transformations
definition: A function T: V→W between vector spaces preserving addition and scalar multiplication.
formula: T(u + v) = T(u) + T(v); T(αu) = αT(u)

name: Inner Product Spaces
definition: Vector space with an inner product (generalized dot product) defining length and angles.
formula: ⟨u,v⟩ properties: linearity, symmetry, positive definiteness

name: Determinants
definition: A scalar value that can be computed from a square matrix, representing volume scaling factor.
formula: det(A) for 2×2: ad-bc; For n×n: cofactor expansion
examples: det(A) = 0 iff A is singular (not invertible)

name: Prime Numbers
definition: Natural numbers greater than 1 that have no positive divisors other than 1 and itself.
formula: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic: every integer > 1 has unique prime factorization

name: Modular Arithmetic
definition: Arithmetic system for integers where numbers wrap around after reaching a modulus.
formula: a ≡ b (mod m) means m divides (a-b)
examples: Fermat's Little Theorem: a^p ≡ a (mod p) for prime p

name: Greatest Common Divisor (GCD)
definition: The largest positive integer that divides both numbers without remainder.
formula: Euclidean algorithm: gcd(a,b) = gcd(b, a mod b)
examples: Bezout's identity: gcd(a,b) = ax + by for some integers x, y

name: Diophantine Equations
definition: Polynomial equations where only integer solutions are sought.
formula: Linear: ax + by = c; Pythagorean: x² + y² = z²
examples: Fermat's Last Theorem: x^n + y^n = z^n has no integer solutions for n>2

name: Chinese Remainder Theorem
definition: System of congruences with coprime moduli has a unique solution modulo the product of moduli.
formula: x ≡ a₁ (mod m₁), x ≡ a₂ (mod m₂), ... has unique solution mod (m₁×m₂×...)

name: Graph Theory Basics
definition: Study of graphs: mathematical structures modeling pairwise relations between objects.
formula: Graph G = (V, E) where V = vertices, E = edges
examples: Complete graph K_n has n vertices, all connected
Tree: connected graph with no cycles

name: Graph Traversal Algorithms
definition: Algorithms for visiting all vertices in a graph systematically.
formula: DFS (Depth-First Search); BFS (Breadth-First Search)
examples: BFS uses queue, finds shortest path in unweighted graphs
DFS uses stack (or recursion), good for cycle detection

name: Shortest Path Algorithms
definition: Algorithms to find minimum-weight path between vertices in weighted graphs.
formula: Dijkstra's algorithm; Bellman-Ford; Floyd-Warshall
examples: Dijkstra: O(E log V) with priority queue

name: Minimum Spanning Tree
definition: Subset of edges that connects all vertices with minimum total weight, no cycles.
formula: Kruskal's algorithm; Prim's algorithm
examples: Kruskal: sort edges, add if no cycle (union-find)
Prim: grow tree from starting vertex

name: Combinatorics - Permutations and Combinations
definition: Counting arrangements (order matters) and selections (order doesn't matter) of objects.
formula: P(n,r) = n!/(n-r)!; C(n,r) = n!/[r!(n-r)!] = (n choose r)
examples: P(5,3) = 60 ways to arrange 3 of 5 objects
C(5,3) = 10 ways to choose 3 of 5 objects

name: Pigeonhole Principle
definition: If n items are placed in m containers and n > m, at least one container has more than one item.
formula: n objects, m holes, n > m → ∃ hole with ⌈n/m⌉ objects
examples: 13 people → at least 2 born in same month
367 people → at least 2 share same birthday
In any set of n+1 integers from {1,2,...,2n}, two are coprime

name: Generating Functions
definition: Power series whose coefficients encode a sequence, used for counting problems.
formula: G(x) = Σ aₙx^n where aₙ is the sequence

name: Propositional Logic
definition: Study of logical statements and their truth values using connectives.
formula: Connectives: ¬ (NOT), ∧ (AND), ∨ (OR), → (IMPLIES), ↔ (IFF)
examples: Law of excluded middle: P ∨ ¬P is always true

name: Predicate Logic
definition: Extension of propositional logic with quantifiers and predicates over domains.
formula: ∀x P(x) (for all); ∃x P(x) (exists)
examples: ∃x (x² = 2) is true in reals, false in rationals

name: Recurrence Relations
definition: Equations defining sequences recursively in terms of previous terms.
formula: aₙ = f(aₙ₋₁, aₙ₋₂, ...); Example: Fibonacci Fₙ = Fₙ₋₁ + Fₙ₋₂
examples: Solving: find characteristic equation, general solution

name: Groups
definition: A set with a binary operation satisfying closure, associativity, identity, and inverse.
formula: Group (G, ∗): ∀a,b∈G: a∗b∈G; (a∗b)∗c=a∗(b∗c); ∃e: a∗e=a; ∀a ∃a⁻¹: a∗a⁻¹=e
examples: Symmetry group of square (D₄) has order 8
Cyclic group Zₙ under addition mod n

name: Rings and Fields
definition: Ring: set with two operations (+, ×) forming abelian group under +. Field: ring where all nonzero elements have multiplicative inverse.
formula: Ring: (R, +, ×); Field: (F, +, ×) with division
examples: Z is a ring but not a field
Z[x] is a polynomial ring over integers

name: Homomorphisms and Isomorphisms
definition: Structure-preserving maps between algebraic structures. Isomorphism is bijective homomorphism.
formula: φ: G→H is homomorphism if φ(a∗b) = φ(a)∗φ(b)
examples: φ: (R,+) → (R⁺,×) by φ(x) = e^x is isomorphism
Kernel of φ: ker(φ) = {g ∈ G : φ(g) = e_H}

name: Quotient Groups
definition: Group formed by partitioning a group by a normal subgroup.
formula: G/N = {gN : g ∈ G} where N is normal subgroup
examples: Quotient by kernel gives isomorphic image

name: Metric Spaces
definition: Set with a distance function (metric) satisfying non-negativity, identity, symmetry, triangle inequality.
formula: d: X×X → R≥0; d(x,y)=0 iff x=y; d(x,y)=d(y,x); d(x,z)≤d(x,y)+d(y,z)
examples: Discrete metric: d(x,y) = 0 if x=y, else 1

name: Continuity and Limits
definition: Function f is continuous at a if lim(x→a) f(x) = f(a).
formula: ε-δ definition: ∀ε>0 ∃δ>0: |x-a|<δ → |f(x)-f(a)|<ε
examples: f(x) = 1/x is continuous on (0,∞) but not at 0
Intermediate Value Theorem for continuous functions

name: Sequences and Series Convergence
definition: Sequence converges to L if terms get arbitrarily close to L. Series converges if partial sums converge.
formula: limₙ→∞ aₙ = L; Series Σaₙ converges if limₙ→∞ Sₙ exists

name: Compactness
definition: A set is compact if every open cover has a finite subcover. In R^n, equivalent to closed and bounded.
formula: Heine-Borel: K ⊂ R^n is compact iff K is closed and bounded
examples: Extreme Value Theorem: continuous f on compact K attains max/min

name: Gradient and Directional Derivatives
definition: Gradient is vector of partial derivatives; directional derivative is rate of change in a given direction.
examples: ∇f points in direction of steepest increase
Used in optimization, machine learning (gradient descent)

name: Divergence and Curl
definition: Divergence measures source/sink strength; curl measures rotation of vector field.
formula: div(F) = ∇·F = ∂Fₓ/∂x + ∂Fᵧ/∂y + ∂Fᶻ/∂z; curl(F) = ∇×F

name: Line and Surface Integrals
definition: Integrals over curves and surfaces in vector fields.
formula: Line: ∫_C F·dr; Surface: ∬_S F·dS
examples: Work done by force F along curve C: W = ∫_C F·dr
Flux through surface S: Φ = ∬_S F·n dS
Green's theorem relates line integral to double integral

name: Conditional Probability
definition: Probability of event A given that event B has occurred.
formula: P(A|B) = P(A∩B)/P(B), P(B) > 0
examples: Independence: P(A|B) = P(A) iff A, B independent

name: Markov Chains
definition: Stochastic process where future state depends only on current state, not history.
formula: P(Xₙ₊₁=j | X₀,...,Xₙ) = P(Xₙ₊₁=j | Xₙ) = Pᵢⱼ

name: Convex Optimization
definition: Optimization of convex objective functions over convex sets; local minimum is global.
formula: min f(x) subject to g(x) ≤ 0, h(x) = 0
examples: Support Vector Machines use convex optimization

name: Lagrange Multipliers
definition: Method for finding extrema of functions subject to equality constraints.
formula: ∇f = λ∇g at extremum of f subject to g(x)=0
examples: Maximize f(x,y) subject to g(x,y) = c
Find closest point on curve to origin
KKT conditions extend to inequality constraints

name: Gradient Descent
definition: Iterative optimization algorithm that moves in direction of steepest descent.
formula: xₙ₊₁ = xₙ - α∇f(xₙ) where α is learning rate
examples: Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) for large datasets

name: Numerical Integration
definition: Approximating definite integrals using discrete samples.
formula: Trapezoidal: ∫f(x)dx ≈ h[f(a)/2 + f(x₁) + ... + f(xₙ₋₁) + f(b)/2]
examples: Monte Carlo integration for high dimensions

name: Root Finding Algorithms
definition: Algorithms to find roots (zeros) of functions numerically.
formula: Newton: xₙ₊₁ = xₙ - f(xₙ)/f'(xₙ); Bisection: repeatedly halve interval

name: Interpolation
definition: Constructing a function passing through given data points.
formula: Lagrange: P(x) = Σ yᵢ Lᵢ(x) where Lᵢ are basis polynomials

name: Taylor Series
definition: Representation of a function as an infinite sum of terms calculated from derivatives at a point.

name: Multiple Integrals
definition: Integration over regions in multiple dimensions.
formula: Double: ∬_R f(x,y) dA; Triple: ∭_V f(x,y,z) dV
examples: ∭_V dV gives volume of region V
Polar: dA = r dr dθ; Spherical: dV = ρ²sin(φ) dρ dφ dθ

name: Green's Theorem
definition: Relates line integral around closed curve to double integral over enclosed region.
formula: ∮_C (P dx + Q dy) = ∬_R (∂Q/∂x - ∂P/∂y) dA

name: Stokes' Theorem
definition: Relates surface integral of curl to line integral around boundary.
formula: ∮_C F·dr = ∬_S (∇×F)·dS
examples: Circulation of F around ∂S equals flux of curl F through S

name: Divergence Theorem (Gauss)
definition: Relates flux through closed surface to divergence over enclosed volume.
formula: ∬_S F·dS = ∭_V (∇·F) dV
examples: Total flux out of volume equals total divergence inside
Gauss's law in electromagnetism: ∬ E·dS = Q/ε₀

name: Complex Functions
definition: Functions from complex numbers to complex numbers.
formula: f(z) = u(x,y) + iv(x,y) where z = x + iy

name: Contour Integration
definition: Integration of complex functions along paths in the complex plane.
formula: ∮_C f(z) dz; Cauchy's theorem: ∮_C f(z) dz = 0 for analytic f
examples: Residue theorem for evaluating real integrals
